text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: synthetic check 'canary-eu-1' (probe group 'canary-eu') has 5 consecutive failures (TTL expired). Window: 3m12s. Paging per policy: infra-oncall
Sam: saw pager, jumping on it now. any indication of broader customer impact?
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident INC12345 created and routed to infra-oncall. Trigger: canary-eu-1 ttl_expiry x5.
Maria: acked in PD — I'm the current infra-oncall, reassign to Raj if needed. Looking at probe dashboard...
Raj: taking it. first glance: canary prober pods show repeated lease renew failures. logs: `error acquiring lease: context deadline exceeded` across eu cluster nodes.
Sam: hmm lease renew -> TTL. did we push any scheduler changes recently?
Raj: not in the prober itself. there was a small NTP job update in EU nodes 20m ago per deploy bot. possible clock skew.
Maria: ops-calendar shows a maintenance window earlier today but should be unrelated. tagging @ops-calendar for maintenance note.
ops-calendar: note: NTP package patch rolled at 2026-03-14T09:20Z on eu-nodes-*.
Sam: ok that matches. canary leases are 60s by default -> if node clocks jumped forward leases appear expired immediately.
Raj: reproducing locally: `kubectl logs -l app=canary-prober -n infra --tail=200` shows: 
```
2026-03-14T09:25:10Z error: failed to renew lease: ttl 0
2026-03-14T09:25:11Z probe skipped: lease expired
```
Maria: mitigation options? quick fix: restart prober pods to re-establish leases. longer fix: bump lease TTL or make renew tolerant to small negative deltas.
Sam: let's do quick restart first to stop pages. Raj, can you rollout restart the prober deployment in eu? `kubectl rollout restart deployment/canary-prober -n infra --context=eu-cluster`
Raj: doing it now.
pagerduty-bot: INC12345 acknowledged by Maria. Auto-escalation paused.
Raj: restarted pods. watching metrics... probe success rate rising. one probe still showing TTL errors but count dropping from 5->1.
Sam: nice. keep an eye for flapping. if stable for 5m we can resolve the PD incident.
Maria: confirming customer-facing paths: no alerts from API gateway or user-facing latency spikes in EU services. seems internal to probe scheduler. marking customer impact: none observed so far.
Raj: logs post-restart: `lease renewed` entries appearing. will keep probes running.
Sam: thanks. follow-up action items?
Maria: immediate: increase lease TTL from 60s -> 120s for EU prober config (can revert after root-cause). medium-term: add retry with clock-skew tolerance + add alert for NTP drift on nodes. long-term: make probe leases resilient to small clock jumps.
Raj: I'll open a PR for TTL bump and a playbook entry for handling TTL-expiry pages. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prober/pull/456 (WIP).
pagerduty-bot: INC12345 status: Resolved by Maria at 2026-03-14T09:31:20Z (note: manual resolve after stability).
Sam: good work. passing on to Katie for postmortem and action tracking. Katie, you ok to own the follow-up?
Katie: yup taking ownership. I'll schedule a 30-min postmortem and include the NTP rotation and rollout notes. will coordinate with infra and release teams.
Maria: leaving a small runbook note in the incident thread: if TTL sustained failures observed -> restart prober pods, check node NTP, escalate to infra-release if NTP patch in maintenance window.
Raj: added logs and timestamps to PR, linking to PD incident and probe traces.
Katie: will also add a detection rule: if synthetic group reports 3+ TTL expiries in 2m, alert infra-release not just infra-oncall.
Sam: thanks everyone. closing slack thread — will wait for postmortem doc but incident considered mitigated and customer impact none. :white_check_mark:
